module_title: Core WTO Agreements: TRIPS, TRIMS, and AoA
introduction: Unlike GATT, the WTO doesn't just manage physical goods. It also regulates ideas, inventions, foreign investments, and agriculture through three very powerful treaties.

core_concepts.title: TRIPS (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights)
core_concepts.description: This agreement prevents the theft of ideas and knowledge. It legally binds member nations to protect 'Patents', 'Copyrights', 'Trademarks', and 'Geographical Indications (GI Tags)'. Because of TRIPS, India had to drastically change its patent laws to recognize product patents.

core_concepts.title: TRIMS (Trade-Related Investment Measures)
core_concepts.description: This agreement deals with foreign 'Investment'. Under TRIMS, a country cannot impose conditions on foreign investors that restrict trade. (For example, India cannot force a foreign mobile company to buy 100% of its batteries locally—this is known as 'Local Content Requirement', which TRIMS prohibits).

core_concepts.title: Agreement on Agriculture (AoA)
core_concepts.description: The AoA aims to establish a fair and market-oriented agricultural trading system. It forces member nations to reduce their 'Agricultural Subsidies' because massive subsidies artificially lower crop prices and ruin the global market.

core_concepts.title: The 3 Subsidy Boxes of AoA
core_concepts.description:
The WTO classifies agricultural subsidies like traffic lights: 
1. Amber Box: 'Trade-distorting' subsidies (e.g., MSP, fertilizer subsidies). These MUST be reduced. 
2. Blue Box: Similar to Amber, but with conditions that limit production. (Allowed but monitored). 
3. Green Box: 'Non-trade distorting' subsidies (e.g., funding for R&D, pest control, environmental protection). No limits; governments can spend as much as they want.

important_entities.name: Compulsory Licensing
important_entities.significance: If a life-saving drug (like a cancer or HIV pill) is too expensive, the WTO allows a government (in a national emergency) to issue a 'Compulsory License' to a local company to manufacture a cheaper generic version, even without the foreign patent owner's consent.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Students constantly mix these up. 
TRIPS = Focus on the 'P' for Patents/Property (Intellectual). 
TRIMS = Focus on the 'M' for Measures/Money (Investments).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Green box = Good for the environment/research. Amber box = Bad for global trade (distorts prices).

exam_strategy_tips: An all-time favorite UPSC Prelims question: 'The terms Amber Box, Blue Box, and Green Box are associated with the affairs of which organization?' Answer: WTO (Agreement on Agriculture).
